## Overview

Adds an opt-in FlashInfer fused SSD scan for Mamba2 prefills (`--mamba-prefill-backend flashinfer`)
and draws the ReplaySSM stochastic-rounding seed once per step instead of once per layer. This PR is
part of a series that brings piecewise CUDA graphs to Mamba2 prefill steps, and it is stacked on
#61497. Tested with #61293 applied, but it does not depend on it. Requires a FlashInfer build with
flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6100, which is not in a release yet.

## Claims

- Up to 1.11x output throughput (OTPS/gpu) over #61497 on 1x B200 with
  Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-NVFP4-W4A4 and MTP=2: 1.06-1.11x at concurrency 8-32, 1.05-1.06x at 64-128
  and 1.03x at 1-4.
- The FlashInfer scan takes 2 launches per layer instead of 5, and host time per scan drops from 174
  us to 97 us (214 us to 125 us for continued prefills with initial states).
- One seed launch per step instead of one per ReplaySSM layer (23 to 1 on this model), in both eager
  mixed steps and the decode CUDA graph.

## Validation

End-to-end serving throughput, before vs after, on the same node, served back-to-back with identical
flags except the new one:

- **Before:** `main` + #61293 + #61497. **After:** the same, plus this PR, with
  `--mamba-prefill-backend flashinfer`.
- **Hardware:** 1x B200, TP1.
- **FlashInfer:** upstream main at `2a2cceab0`, which includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6100
  (`cu_seqlens` support) and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6206 (Cake SSD prefill performance).
- **Workload:** SPEED-Bench `throughput_1k`, `low_entropy` category (512 prompts),
  `max_tokens` 200, served through aiperf.
  - Warm-up: 256 requests at concurrency 128, discarded.
  - Then the full 512-prompt dataset at each concurrency from 128 down to 1.
  - Concurrency 64 and 128 were run 2 more times; those rows are the mean of 3 runs.

Values are OTPS/gpu (output tokens/s per GPU):

| Concurrency | Before PR | After PR | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 804 | 824 | 1.03x |
| 2 | 1324 | 1366 | 1.03x |
| 4 | 2033 | 2099 | 1.03x |
| 8 | 3117 | 3305 | 1.06x |
| 16 | 4694 | 5094 | 1.09x |
| 32 | 7383 | 8189 | 1.11x |
| 64 | 12110 | 12804 | 1.06x |
| 128 | 17290 | 18176 | 1.05x |

Mid concurrencies have the most prefill and mixed-batch interruptions, so they gain the most; the
effect is smaller at low and high concurrency.

Accuracy: GPQA-diamond through NeMo Gym on 1x GB300, TP1, MTP=2 (198 questions x 8 repeats, thinking on,
temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95), with the serve command below plus `--max-model-len 262144
--reasoning-parser nemotron_v3`. pass@1, mean over the 8 repeats ± standard error:

- No prefix reuse (as below): 76.45 ± 0.53%
- Prefix reuse (`--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, no ReplaySSM): 76.58 ± 0.93%

<details>
<summary>Serve and client commands</summary>

`--mamba-prefill-backend flashinfer` selects this PR's scan for prefills; `--mamba-backend
flashinfer` only selects the decode state update. The Before run used the same command without
`--mamba-prefill-backend`.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
MODEL=${MODEL:?path or HF id of the Nemotron-3.5-Lightning NVFP4 W4A4 checkpoint}
NUMA_NODE=${NUMA_NODE:?NUMA node local to the GPU}
CAPTURE_SIZES='[1,2,4,8,16,24,32,40,48,56,64,72,80,88,96,104,112,120,128,136,144,152,160,168,176,184,192,200,208,216,224,232,240,248,256,272,288,304,320,336,352,368,384,400,416,432,448,464,480,496,512,528,544,560,576,592,608,624,640,656,672,688,704,720,736,752,768,784,800,816,832,848,864,880,896,912,928,944,960,976,992,1008,1024,1152,1280,1408,1536,1664,1792,1920,2048,2560,3072,3584,4096,5120,6144,7168,8192,10240,12288,14336,16384,18432,20480,22528,24576,26624,28672,30720,32768]'

vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name nemotron-3.5-lightning \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --async-scheduling \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2,"moe_backend":"flashinfer_trtllm"}' \
  --mamba-cache-mode none \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer \
  --mamba-prefill-backend flashinfer \
  --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
  --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding \
  --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \
  --use-replayssm \
  --compilation-config "{\"mode\":3,\"cudagraph_mode\":\"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE\",\"max_cudagraph_capture_size\":32768,\"cudagraph_capture_sizes\":${CAPTURE_SIZES}}" \
  --numa-bind --numa-bind-nodes "$NUMA_NODE" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001
```

Client, run once per concurrency level:

```bash
aiperf profile \
  --model nemotron-3.5-lightning --tokenizer "$MODEL" --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --endpoint-type chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --streaming --use-legacy-max-tokens \
  --url http://localhost:8001 \
  --input-file "$SPEED_BENCH_1K_LOW_ENTROPY_JSONL" \
  --extra-inputs max_tokens:200 --extra-inputs skip_special_tokens:false \
  --random-seed 1234 --use-server-token-count \
  --concurrency "$CONC" --request-count 512 --num-dataset-entries 512
```

</details>

## Details

Mamba2 prefills run the chunked SSD scan as 5 Triton launches per layer (cumsum, chunk state, state
passing, bmm, chunk scan). Continued prefills add a gather and a `torch.where` for their initial
states. In eager prefill and mixed steps, these launches and their host overhead add directly to
step latency. FlashInfer's fused SSD (`SSDCombined`, Cake backend) runs the scan in 2 launches from
the packed-varlen `cu_seqlens` and derives its chunk metadata on the device.

Changes:

- `--mamba-prefill-backend {triton,flashinfer}` (`MambaConfig.prefill_backend`, default `triton`).
  Prefills that store Mamba checkpoints need every chunk state, so they keep the Triton scan.
- `mamba_chunk_scan_flashinfer()` (`ops/ssd_flashinfer.py`):
  - gathers initial states (one launch) only when some sequence has one, and otherwise starts from
    a zero state;
  - runs one `SSDCombined` runner per (stream, heads, groups, state dtype, initial states), so final
    states come out in the cache dtype;
  - scatters each final state into its cache slot.
- The gather and scatter kernels do not specialize `indices_ptr` on alignment. Its alignment changes
  with the number of decode rows, so this avoids new compiles while serving.
- The mixer keeps a bfloat16 copy of `D` for FlashInfer, refreshed when the parameter changes.
- The backend needs SM100/SM103, bfloat16 activations, head dim 64 and state size 128 (the shapes
  FlashInfer compiles). `MambaConfig` and `MambaMixer2` reject other setups, and the SSD warm-up runs
  both FlashInfer variants.
- ReplaySSM seed: with `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding`, each FlashInfer ReplaySSM layer
  drew its Philox seed with its own `torch.randint`. The layers now read their seeds from slots of
  one shared buffer, which the first layer refreshes with a single `random_()` per step. Every layer
  still gets an independent seed each step.

---
